additions.reason: The letter vav IS a bechina of tosefet kedusha and shmirat habrit. The source text (§3) explicitly says: 'kol makom she-ne'emar vav, hu mosif... bechinas tosefot kedusha, haynu shmirat habrit.' The vav adds/extends holiness — it is the structural embodiment of the positive side of covenant (the letter that adds, just as the covenant adds holiness). Currently in the dataset as an eitza edge (id=71: vav → kavod), but the bechina content ('vav IS tosefet kedusha / shmirat habrit') is not captured as a bechina edge.
additions.source_quote: כָּל מָקוֹם שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר וָא"ו, הוּא מוֹסִיף, הַיְנוּ בְּחִינַת תּוֹסְפוֹת קְדֻשָּׁה, הַיְנוּ שְׁמִירַת הַבְּרִית

additions.reason: The dew of lights (tal orot) IS a bechina of the vav-of-kavod: the 39 lights included in the vav. The source text (§4) says 'ze ha-or... bechinas tal orot ha-kelulim ba-vav shel kavod.' Tal orot is also the gematria of the milui (full spelling) of the first three letters of the divine Name. This belongs in Package 1 as it is equivalent to the 39 lights (l"t orot) of the built Tabernacle.
additions.source_quote: וְאוֹר הַזֶּה הוּא בְּחִינַת טַל אוֹרוֹת הַכְּלוּלִים בַּוָּא"ו שֶׁל כָּבוֹד

additions.reason: 'Boaz' IS the brit: 'bo az, bo tukpa' (the brit is called Boaz because 'bo' = in it, 'az' = strength). The source text (§4) gives Boaz as the name of the brit, encompassing both the 39 lights (shmirat habrit) and the 39 melachot (its violation). This is a bechina: the name Boaz IS a description of what the brit essentially IS.
additions.source_quote: וְעַל שֵׁם זֶה נִקְרָא בְּרִית בֹּעַז (תִּיקּוּן לא) – בּוֹ עַז, בּוֹ תֻּקְפָּא

additions.reason: The seven houses of idolatry IS the bechina of gadlut (pride). The source text (§7) states: 'gadlut hu bechinas sheva batei idolatry' — pride is the root cause of exile and is equated with the seven idolatrous establishments that caused Israel's exile. This belongs in Package 4 (pride/idolatry) as it IS another expression of the same reality.
additions.source_quote: גַּדְלוּת... שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת שֶׁבַע בָּתֵּי עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה כַּנַּ"ל

additions.reason: Divine honor (kavod) is structurally equivalent to dibbur in this Torah. The Torah explicitly states 'ikar bechinas ha-dibbur hu mi-kavod' (§2): the essence of speech flows from kavod. The verse 'mi hu zeh melech ha-kavod — haynu malkhut peh' explicitly identifies kavod with the mouth/speech. While kavod features in many eitza edges for this Torah (kavod → dibbur ha-meir), the bechina 'kavod IS malkhut peh / dibbur' is not captured as a bechina edge in the dataset.
additions.source_quote: כִּי עִקַּר בְּחִינַת הַדִּבּוּר הוּא מִכָּבוֹד, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (תְּהִלִּים כ"ד): מִי הוּא זֶה מֶלֶךְ הַכָּבוֹד – הַיְנוּ מַלְכוּת פֶּה

additions.reason: LM2 Torah 11 is entirely about prayer (tefilla). The LM2 text (line 2) explicitly equates prayer with siach: 'ha-tefilla nikre'et sicha, bechinas siach ha-sadeh.' This is a direct bechina: prayer IS the speech/conversation of the field. This concept from LM2/11 has no bechina edge in the dataset.

The speech/plants of the field IS a bechina of prayer. From LM2 Torah 11 (line 2): the grasses give power to prayer; prayer is called sicha because of siach ha-sadeh. The field plants ARE prayer's supporting force — two expressions of the same spiritual assistance. This concept from LM2/11 has no bechina edge in the dataset.
additions.source_quote: כָּל שִׂיחַ הַשָּׂדֶה נוֹתְנִין כֹּחַ וְסִיּוּעַ בִּתְפִלָּתוֹ

additions.reason: The grasses/herbs of the field participate in strengthening prayer when one prays in the field. From LM2/11 (line 1): 'kol ha-asavim kulam ba'in b'tokh ha-tefilla u-msayyin lo.' They are neutral structural elements (natural phenomena) that can serve the domain of prayer/speech. Not in the dataset as a bechina edge.
additions.source_quote: כָּל הָעֲשָׂבִים כֻּלָּם בָּאִין בְּתוֹךְ הַתְּפִלָּה, וּמְסַיְּעִין לוֹ

additions.reason: The produce of the earth (yevul ha-aretz) gives power to prayer even when not praying in the field — through food and drink consumed by the person. LM2/11 (line 3) explicitly connects failure of yevul ha-aretz to failure of prayer support. Not in the dataset.

analysis_notes.dataset_ambiguity_note: The dataset has no 'volume' field. All 37 reference=11 bechina edges match the content of LM1 Torah 11 ('Ani Hashem Hu Shmi' — about kavod, brit, dibbur, yichuda). LM2 Torah 11 ('field prayer / siach hasadeh') is a 6-line Torah with no bechina edges in the current dataset. The additions above include concepts from both texts. Future data entry should add a 'volume' field to disambiguate.
